newsitem.title: GERMANY: Major oil/meals importers seen raising purchases.
newsitem.headline: Major oil/meals importers seen raising purchases.

text.p: Major buyers of vegetable oils and oilmeals are likely to step up their purchases in the 1997/98 (Oct/Sept) season, the Oil World newsletter said.
In oils and fats, it attributed the increases to lower carry-in stocks, lower domestic production and rising demand, especially in China, India and Iran.
Slight increases were forecast for Taiwan and Egypt while Bangladeshi requirements were seen steady and South Korea was expected to buy less from the world market in the new season.
Oil World, after studying data from the seven countries estimated that together, they may import 10.17 million tonnes of oils in 1997/98, 17 percent more than in 1996/97.
It said palm oil would gain most from the increased import demand, followed by rape, soybean and sunflower oils.
In meals, the rise in demand was put down to an expansion of livestock rearing and fish farming.
The seven countries together were forecast to import 11.67 million tonnes in 1997/98, 37 percent more than previously, led by China, South Korea and Iran and benefiting mostly soymeal.
Taiwan should cut its import because of a foot-and-mouth disease outbreak while prospective imports by Bangladesh and India were negligible. --Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom +49-40-41903275
